stem:
Kiara's uncle has diabetes. The doctor links his risk to diet, low activity, and asks for regular checkups and ongoing care, not a one-time course of medicine alone.

Which two claims correctly explain non-communicable disease risk and control?

options.text: Lifestyle, diet, and environment can raise risk, so healthier habits and early diagnosis help control the disease.
One short course of diabetes medicine gives permanent control with no further care needed.
Continuous care and monitoring remain important after diagnosis, even when he looks well on some days.
A healthy diet and regular exercise prevent every non-communicable disease in every person.

teacher.key_rationale: Non-communicable disease risk links to lifestyle, diet, and environment; control needs early diagnosis and continuous care. Ending care after one medicine course, or claiming lifestyle prevents every case, miss that hinge.
